---
title: The Lantern Keeper
author: Mara Vell
language: en
era: 1920s coastal Maine
---

## The Light

The keeper climbed the spiral stair twice each night, once at dusk to
wake the lantern and once before dawn to let it sleep again.

She had done this for thirty years, and in that time had spoken to the
sea more often than to any person, and found it the better listener.

## The Fog

When the fog came it came all at once, swallowing the beam whole, and
then the light was not for seeing by but only for being heard.

On such nights she rang the bell herself, slowly, and counted the ships
by the answers that came back across the water, faint and grateful.

## The Wreck

There was one winter she did not speak of, when a ship came in too fast
and the bell was not enough, and the sea kept what it had taken.

After that she climbed the stair a third time each night, at the hour of
the wreck, and stood a while at the glass, keeping a watch on nothing.
